plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 14.2.10
plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to find the volume of the tetrahedron bounded by the coordinate planes and the plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y using a double integral. The figure contains two linked diagrams. Left: a 3D perspective showing the tetrahedron in xyz-space with vertices at (0, 0, 4), (1, 0, 0), and (0, 2, 0), bounded above by the plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y (labeled on the slanted face) with the base region R labeled. Right (inset): the 2D base region R in the xy-plane, a right triangle with vertices at (0, 0), (1, 0), and (0, 2), bounded by the x-axis, y-axis, and the line y = 2 - 2x; a red vertical strip illustrates the inner integration limits from y = 0 to y = 2 - 2x. An arrow connects the two diagrams. The figure establishes the correspondence between the 3D tetrahedron and the triangular base R over which the iterated double integral is set up.

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The triangular region R in the xy-plane is the projection of the tetrahedron onto the base, and the same limits describe both views
A vertical integration strip at x=c in the 2D region corresponds to a fixed-x slice of the 3D volume whose top edge lies on z = 4 - 4x - 2y
Rotating the tetrahedron reveals that the slanted triangular face is a plane above the triangular base region, not a separate 2D triangle

demo_steps.title: Start with the tetrahedron
demo_steps.narration: The solid is bounded by the coordinate planes and the plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y. Its intercepts occur at x=1, y=2, and z=4.

demo_steps.title: Project onto the xy-plane
demo_steps.narration: Switching to the base view shows the projection R: the triangle bounded by x=0, y=0, and y = 2 - 2x.

demo_steps.title: Link an integration strip to a slice
demo_steps.narration: In linked view, dragging the red strip through R updates the matching fixed-x cross-section on the 3D plane. The strip height is y = 2 - 2x, while the surface height is z = 4 - 4x - 2y.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use actual mathematical coordinates as world coordinates for the 3D solid: O=(0,0,0), X=(1,0,0), Y=(0,2,0), Z=(0,0,4). The tetrahedron fits in x∈[0,1], y∈[0,2], z∈[0,4]; add axis arrows extending slightly beyond the intercepts: x to about 1.25, y to about 2.35, z to about 4.45. Match the source orientation in the default axonometric view: z appears vertical upward, y extends to the right, and x recedes diagonally down-left. The slanted triangular top face is exactly z=4-4x-2y over R. Base region R is the xy-plane triangle 0≤x≤1, 0≤y≤2-2x. For the draggable strip use parameter c clamped to [0,1], default c≈0.45. In the 2D panel draw the red strip from (c,0) to (c,2-2c). In the 3D panel draw the corresponding highlighted top cross-section from (c,0,4-4c) to (c,2-2c,0), plus a very translucent red triangular curtain with vertices (c,0,0), (c,2-2c,0), and (c,0,4-4c). Use pale cyan fills #c7e9e8 with opacity around 0.45 for faces and #bde4e2 opacity around 0.6 for R; teal/cyan edges and dots #22bfc1; black axes and labels #222222; red strip/slice #ff4b4b; optional curved arrow fill pale cream #ffe7ad with gray outline #aaaaaa. Keep 2D base-panel scale equal in x and y so vertices (0,0), (1,0), and (0,2) form the same tall right triangle as the source inset.
interactionPlan.notes: Implement panelView by showing either a full 3D scene, a full 2D orthographic base diagram, or a linked split layout with the 3D tetrahedron on the left and the 2D base on the right. In linked split view, keep the two panels synchronized through the single strip parameter c. Use raycasting or 2D pointer projection to drag the red strip horizontally; ignore vertical pointer movement and clamp c to [0,1]. Orbit should affect only the 3D tetrahedron camera, not the 2D base panel. Render labels as sprites or CSS2D objects that remain readable during orbit. Use transparent double-sided triangular meshes for tetrahedron faces so the red slice remains visible through the solid.

plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 14.2.10
plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to find the volume of the tetrahedron bounded by the coordinate planes and the plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y using a double integral. The figure contains two linked diagrams. Left: a 3D perspective showing the tetrahedron in xyz-space with vertices at (0, 0, 4), (1, 0, 0), and (0, 2, 0), bounded above by the plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y (labeled on the slanted face) with the base region R labeled. Right (inset): the 2D base region R in the xy-plane, a right triangle with vertices at (0, 0), (1, 0), and (0, 2), bounded by the x-axis, y-axis, and the line y = 2 - 2x; a red vertical strip illustrates the inner integration limits from y = 0 to y = 2 - 2x. An arrow connects the two diagrams. The figure establishes the correspondence between the 3D tetrahedron and the triangular base R over which the iterated double integral is set up.

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The triangular region R in the xy-plane is the projection of the tetrahedron onto the base, and the same limits describe both views
A vertical integration strip at x=c in the 2D region corresponds to a fixed-x slice of the 3D volume whose top edge lies on z = 4 - 4x - 2y
Rotating the tetrahedron reveals that the slanted triangular face is a plane above the triangular base region, not a separate 2D triangle

demo_steps.title: Start with the tetrahedron
demo_steps.narration: The solid is bounded by the coordinate planes and the plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y. Its intercepts occur at x=1, y=2, and z=4.

demo_steps.title: Project onto the xy-plane
demo_steps.narration: Switching to the base view shows the projection R: the triangle bounded by x=0, y=0, and y = 2 - 2x.

demo_steps.title: Link an integration strip to a slice
demo_steps.narration: In linked view, dragging the red strip through R updates the matching fixed-x cross-section on the 3D plane. The strip height is y = 2 - 2x, while the surface height is z = 4 - 4x - 2y.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use actual mathematical coordinates as world coordinates for the 3D solid: O=(0,0,0), X=(1,0,0), Y=(0,2,0), Z=(0,0,4). The tetrahedron fits in x∈[0,1], y∈[0,2], z∈[0,4]; add axis arrows extending slightly beyond the intercepts: x to about 1.25, y to about 2.35, z to about 4.45. Match the source orientation in the default axonometric view: z appears vertical upward, y extends to the right, and x recedes diagonally down-left. The slanted triangular top face is exactly z=4-4x-2y over R. Base region R is the xy-plane triangle 0≤x≤1, 0≤y≤2-2x. For the draggable strip use parameter c clamped to [0,1], default c≈0.45. In the 2D panel draw the red strip from (c,0) to (c,2-2c). In the 3D panel draw the corresponding highlighted top cross-section from (c,0,4-4c) to (c,2-2c,0), plus a very translucent red triangular curtain with vertices (c,0,0), (c,2-2c,0), and (c,0,4-4c). Use pale cyan fills #c7e9e8 with opacity around 0.45 for faces and #bde4e2 opacity around 0.6 for R; teal/cyan edges and dots #22bfc1; black axes and labels #222222; red strip/slice #ff4b4b; optional curved arrow fill pale cream #ffe7ad with gray outline #aaaaaa. Keep 2D base-panel scale equal in x and y so vertices (0,0), (1,0), and (0,2) form the same tall right triangle as the source inset.
interactionPlan.notes: Implement panelView by showing either a full 3D scene, a full 2D orthographic base diagram, or a linked split layout with the 3D tetrahedron on the left and the 2D base on the right. In linked split view, keep the two panels synchronized through the single strip parameter c. Use raycasting or 2D pointer projection to drag the red strip horizontally; ignore vertical pointer movement and clamp c to [0,1]. Orbit should affect only the 3D tetrahedron camera, not the 2D base panel. Render labels as sprites or CSS2D objects that remain readable during orbit. Use transparent double-sided triangular meshes for tetrahedron faces so the red slice remains visible through the solid.
